# The bench with a two-preset roster, so an arm can name an agent composition
# instead of only a model route and an implementer. `bench` composes no row of
# its own and leaves the cell agent exactly as the base composition builds it;
# `bench-craft` adds the fixture's three craft skills as a second skill root,
# the same catalog the with-craft-skills overlay mounts for every cell. The two
# presets therefore differ in the catalog and the bodies the model may load and
# in nothing else, which is what makes a pair over one route a measurement of
# the composition. The roots are found from the repository root above
# `baseUrl`, as the craft-skills overlay does.
- id: base
  name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
  config:
    path: ../cordis.yml

# `includeUserRoot: false` keeps the machine's own `<dshHome>/.agent-presets`
# out of the roster: a bench arm names a preset by id, and a home directory that
# happened to supply that id would silently decide what the arm measured.
- id: agent-presets
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
  config:
    default: bench
    includeUserRoot: false
    roots:
      - trust: system
        path: !!js |
            (() => {
              const { fileURLToPath } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:url')
              const { existsSync } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:fs')
              const { dirname, join } = process.getBuiltinModule('node:path')
              let dir = fileURLToPath(baseUrl)
              while (!existsSync(join(dir, 'pnpm-workspace.yaml'))) {
                const parent = dirname(dir)
                if (parent === dir) throw new Error('proving-ground-bench overlay: repository root not found above ' + baseUrl)
                dir = parent
              }
              return join(dir, 'examples', 'headless-agent', 'tests', 'fixtures', 'proving-ground-bench', 'presets')
            })()

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The validation instrument: one model-facing `standard_author` tool with which a validator derives a completion standard of weighted cases from a reference program, before any implementation of the task exists. # Process transcript dataset

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

## What this is

This dataset is the process transcripts of an AI-assisted build of the DeepSeek Harness fork, produced by Claude Code sessions: one orchestrating session (`agents.jsonl` record with `kind: "orchestrator"`) plus 116 background subagent sessions it spawned (`kind: "subagent"`), covering every message, tool call, and token count either session logged.

- `agents.jsonl` - one record per transcript: timing, turn/tool-call counts and breakdown, token usage, prompt/response excerpts, commit shas mentioned in the final assistant message, and files touched via Edit/Write/MultiEdit.
- `messages.jsonl` - one record per conversational message across every transcript, in order, with per-message text, tool calls, and tool-result sizes.
- `stats.json` - corpus totals (transcripts, messages, tool calls by name, tokens by kind, wall time) and the distribution of subagent durations.

## What was removed

- **Tool result bodies.** `messages.jsonl` records only the character count of each tool result (`toolResultChars`), never its content; the raw tree next to this dataset keeps the bodies.
- **Secrets.** Any value shaped like a credential - an `sk-`, `ghp_`, or `AKIA`-prefixed token, a `Bearer ` header value, or any other 32-or-more character hex/base64-looking run - is replaced with `[REDACTED]` everywhere this dataset includes text: message text, prompt/response excerpts, and tool-call input excerpts.
- **Non-transcript files.** `subagents/` held 116 transcript-shaped files; 116 of them are genuine Claude Code JSONL subagent transcripts (every line parses as JSON and at least one line is a real user/assistant message). 0 were plain-text captures of other tool output, 0 were JSON without any conversation, and 0 were empty. None of these is represented in `agents.jsonl` or `messages.jsonl`.

## Data quality notes

- 0 of the 116 subagent transcript files were symlinks into a live Claude Code project directory rather than frozen copies; a subagent still running at export time shows more lines on a later re-run of `transcripts-to-dataset.mjs` than it did here.
- 2 subagent transcript(s) end mid-action: the last recorded line is a tool call with no accompanying text and no result, rather than a closing report - id(s): `a1fe58841b58bf1ff`, `ac1d0180b6ef3cf0a`. For these, `finalAssistantExcerpt` and `commitShasMentioned` reflect that the transcript stops there, not that the agent produced no final report.

## Provenance

- Build/session id: `f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce`
- Raw transcripts: `data/transcripts/2026-09-06-build/raw`
- Export date: 2026-09-19
- Harness repo branch at export time: `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`

I read the tree at HEAD `c0efe64a3` on `claude/coding-agent-harness-u9l4gt`, which is 425 commits ahead of its master merge-base. I ran no tests, servers or generators. The roster "liveness" numbers come from re-implementing the feed's mapping logic in a read-only script over the session files on disk. Another session was writing to the tree while I read it. It added an untracked `data/code-safety/2026-09-22-nodegoat-4-improved/` and modified `data/knowledge/code-safety/injection/SKILL.md`. I mark anything taken from those files as uncommitted.

**Bottom line:** the repo holds one real software build by its own departments: a 447-line CLI, and the built code was never committed. The 147-agent roster is a set of generated JSON records whose presets are unit-test stubs. The only true multi-agent build on file is Claude Code building this repo, not DeepSeek Harness.

## 1. The "program": how a multi-agent program is composed

**What it is.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-program` (`ctx.programs`). From `/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/improvement/program/README.md:5`: "A program is a frozen spec, one program session holding `program/*` events, one department session and git worktree per goal, and one integration session whose certificate over the merged head is what a release claims."
- The orchestrator is deterministic TypeScript (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/improvement/program/src/index.ts`, 1,416 lines), not an LLM manager.
- README:64: "The service is the department's validator."

**How departments are declared.** Each department is an entry in `ProgramSpec.goals[]` with `key, objective, preset, isolation, budget, dependsOn, checks` (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/improvement/program/src/types.ts:34-49`; implementer choice at :85-93).
- These specs are written in TypeScript inside each fixture's driver, not in `cordis.yml`.

**How work is delegated.** A goal starts once its dependencies certify. The service creates a worktree on `<branchPrefix>/<programId>/<key>`, a session, `program/member`, `budget/caps`, a goal and a standard (README:62).
- With `implementer: route`, the service sends the objective as a user turn (`index.ts:1119`).
- With `implementer: subagent`, it makes one `ctx.subagents.start` call per attempt (`index.ts:1138-1165`; README:70).

**How results are merged.** The service creates an `@integration` worktree and runs `git merge --no-ff` for each branch in dependency order. It refuses a branch that moved after certification (`index.ts:805-822`; README:78).
- The integration standard is the integration checks plus one `gate-<n>` check per gate (README:80).
- The integration session is barred from reading the department worktrees (README:82).
- There is no semantic merge unless the merged head fails its checks.

**Retries and attempts.** The loop is at `index.ts:1187-1232`. Each round:
1. Deliver the prompt.
2. Run `git status --porcelain`. If the worktree is dirty, issue an `<uncommitted_work>` directive (`index.ts:286`) and spend the round.
3. Otherwise run the checks through the shell. Pass means certify. Fail means a `<checks_failed>` directive (`index.ts:275`) and another round.
- When rounds run out, the goal is recorded `failed`: "no certificate after N rounds" (`index.ts:1109`).
- A blocked goal waits for an operator (README:112).
- Bench cells use a different mechanism: the environment runner's attempt ladder (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/improvement/environment-runner/README.md:53-61`).
- Nothing checks that a goal's checks fail on the base revision. The repo records one vacuous pass: "the goals certified only because the fixture's checks pass on the untouched base" (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/.agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-09-07-roles-matrix-on-the-subscription.md:20`).

**Where the run log lives.**
- The ledger is session `program-<digest>` (`program/start|goal|integration|resume|end`, README:48-56).
- Departments are `program-<digest>-<key>`; the integration is `program-<digest>-~0040integration`.
- The driver prints one result line to `stdout.jsonl`.
- Runs are recorded by `/home/user/deepseek-harness/data/proving-ground/tools/record-run.mjs` or `/home/user/deepseek-harness/data/code-safety/tools/record-run.mjs` into `manifest.json`, `result.json` and `sessions/`.
- Live runs sit in `.code-safety/<id>/` and `.proving-ground/runs/<id>/{plan.json,run.log,.sessions}`.

**Signoffs.** `requireSignoff: true` is set, but each driver writes both "human" signatures itself before `programs.start`, over placeholder digests.
- csv-tools `driver.ts:32`: `const ARTEFACT = 'c'.repeat(64)`; `driver.ts:188`: `principal: { kind: 'human', id: 'csv-tools-client', … }`.

## 2. The 147-agent roster

**Where it is generated and shown.**
- `/home/user/deepseek-harness/scripts/enterprise-roster.ts` (`pnpm run roster`) writes `/home/user/deepseek-harness/data/enterprise/roster.json`.
- `/home/user/deepseek-harness/scripts/harness-feed.ts` serves `GET /roster` on port 4711 (`pnpm run feed`) with live status overlaid.
- `/home/user/deepseek-harness/apps/command-deck` renders it. A snapshot is in `/home/user/deepseek-harness/apps/command-deck/public/fixtures/roster.json`, published to GitHub Pages.

**What an "agent" is.** A JSON record with `id, role, division, route, preset, skills, tools, source, status` (`enterprise-roster.ts:46-74`). It is not a plugin, a mountable preset, or a session.
- `ROSTER_AGENT_COUNT = 147` (:119) is filled from fixed quotas per division (:129-140), built from repository artifacts:
  - one "steward" per package README;
  - one "verifier" per `verify-*.ts` script, on route `codex` (:552-570);
  - one "judge" per CI gate id, on route `codex` (:578-612);
  - one "skill-keeper" per skill directory;
  - 36 code-safety reviewers, from 6 departments × 6 languages. They include Java, Go, PHP and Mobile, for which the repo has no scanner (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/data/enterprise/README.md:30`).
- The relationships between agents are assigned by index arithmetic, e.g. :838 `verifiers[index % verifiers.length]`.

**The presets are stubs.** Every seat's preset is `coding` (47 seats) or `reviewing` (100 seats).
- The comment at :61 calls them "the two presets this repository ships as fixtures".
- They exist only as unit-test fixtures under `/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/subagent/subagent-in-process-driver/tests/fixtures/presets/{coding,reviewing}/`. Each contains a single dummy tool (`preset_only` or `reviewing_only`).
- The real shipped presets are the six in `/home/user/deepseek-harness/apps/cli/config/agent-presets/`: code, cordis, judge, minimal, standard, validator. The word "roster" means two different things in this repo.

**The routes were never used.** Seats name 74 `deepseek-official`, 25 `codex`, 36 OpenRouter free-tier and 12 `claude-code` routes.
- Of the 830 recorded sessions that carry a request header, 801 ran on `claude-code` and 29 on OpenRouter free models.
- None ran on `deepseek-official` and none on `codex`.
- The feed admits this (`harness-feed.ts:943-944`): "a review runs on the operator's Claude Code route while the seats name their default routes."

**Live status is guessed.** `mapSessionToAgentId` (`harness-feed.ts:920-935`) works like this:
- Any `program-<hex>` session is assigned to a code-safety seat (:949-961).
- Otherwise it matches on provider/model, then on a role or division keyword in the system prompt, then takes the first seat in the pool, then falls back to `roster.agents[0]` (:1028).

Replaying that logic over all 1,598 session files on disk:
- Only 16 of 147 seats ever leave `defined`.
- 707 sessions collapse onto one seat and 541 onto the fallback seat.
- The committed deck fixture shows 131 defined, 14 certified, 2 failed.
- "Secrets × Mobile Reviewer" shows as certified because OpenRouter coding cells (`code:path-normalize`, `code:csv-codec`) certified.
- The csv-tools ledger and integration sessions would be shown as "Code Safety Program Lead".

**The deck's Judging gate is decorative.** `/home/user/deepseek-harness/apps/command-deck/deck/pipeline.ts:36-41` draws a Judging gate, and :72 only routes `division === 'judging'` events to it. No recorded session maps to a judging seat, so no real event ever reaches that gate.

**Verdict: a projection, not runnable compositions.** The data README is honest: "It is never the count of agents currently running" (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/data/enterprise/README.md:9`). The client demo script overstates it: `/home/user/deepseek-harness/docs/code-safety-poc.md:9` says "Every agent on the graph derives from a definition in this repository (a preset, a plan, a fixture, a note)".

## 4. Workflows

**`.agents/workflows/` does not exist.** `/home/user/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md:51` still says `.agents/` holds "Agent workflows and Agent Notes". Only `notes/` and `skills/` are there, and git history has no such path.

**What exists.** `/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/workflow` has four packages, documented in `/home/user/deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/workflow.md`:
- `workflow` provides `ctx.workflowEngine`;
- `workflow-worker-thread` runs one worker thread per run;
- `tool-workflow` lets the model write a JavaScript script using `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`, `phase()`, `log()`;
- `tool-ralph` gives one fixed objective to a series of fresh child agents.

**What invokes them.** The model does, through the `workflow` and `ralph` tools. They ship in the standard and code presets (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/apps/cli/config/agent-presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml:226-230`) and in the base and web-app bundles. Ralph is to be used "ONLY when the direct human explicitly asks" (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/packages/workflow/tool-ralph/README.md:47`).

**Limits.**
- Ralph: "Completion is worker self-declaration" (tool-ralph README:88). It runs only in the foreground and never retries a failed round.
- Workflows: journaling and resume are deferred (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-05-dynamic-workflows.md:59-60`).
- "Durable workflow runs" are display records in the chat log (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/docs/subsystems/workflow.md:122-128`). A run does not survive a restart.

**Snapshot coverage.** Two keyless replays exist, and both only prove the wiring:
- headless `ralph-loop` (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/headless-agent/tests/headless.snapshot.ts:66-67, :950-991`): "Run a two-round fresh-agent Ralph loop to prove the shipped headless integration."
- ACP `workflow-run` (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/acp-agent/tests/acp.snapshot.ts:493`): one child that replies `WF_CHILD_OK`.

**Program coverage.** No snapshot covers programs; that was explicitly rejected (program-workflow-builds-software.md:43). Programs have only keyless e2e tests (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/headless-agent/tests/program-csv-tools.e2e.ts`, `program-code-safety.e2e.ts`) and unit specs.

**Workflows and programs are not connected.** Program departments are single agent loops. The Goal-2 design, "W2 — Certificate-first software factory" (`/home/user/deepseek-harness/.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md:81-107`), is itself still a proposed note. ## Top 10 gaps

1. **No convincing build record.** One 447-line CLI with a pre-written spec and tests, and the delivered code was not committed. Missing: a committed deliverable, a held-out multi-module task, and the program that builds something for this repo under its own gates.
2. **The roster is not runnable.** Seats point at unit-test stub presets and at routes (`deepseek-official`, `codex`) that were never used. Live status is guessed by heuristics and mislabels sessions.
3. **No reviewer role anywhere in the build path.** There is no code review by an agent, and the `review-acceptance` signoff exists in the vocabulary but nothing reads it.
4. **Tests are handed in by the script.** No agent writes tests inside a program, and nothing checks that a goal's tests fail before the work starts, so a goal can pass without doing anything.
5. **No ship step.** Release is a local merge; there is no push, PR, package or deploy, and the release is "signed" before the work begins.
6. **CI never ran.** The quality gates were never enforced on any agent-written commit on GitHub.
7. **The multi-agent tools are unused in real work.** No recorded run uses subagent, workflow or Ralph calls, and no program has ever delegated a department to another agent.
8. **The one comparison runs against the pitch.** On NodeGoat a single model pass found more issues than the six-department enterprise (15 vs 13 of 18), with a single run per side; the claim that the enterprise wins at scale has no measurement behind it.
9. **Everything ran on Claude, not DeepSeek.** Every program run used the operator's Claude subscription, with one model for all departments, and the model is not recorded per department.
10. **Programs are hard to run and hard to trace.** You need a hand-written TypeScript driver per program; there is no CLI entry, the scorekeeper does not count programs (program README:108), only one program runs per process, commits carry no department identity, and there is no transcript after 2026-09-19.
